speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old male. The patient reports the sudden onset of abdominal pain while playing football two hours ago. He has a past medical history significant only for asthma. Additionally, his social history is notable for unprotected sex with four partners in the past month.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset abdominal pain. I also have No history of similar episodes, Pain started while playing football. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; please ignore the previous comment about multiple sclerosis as that does not align with your acute abdominal presentation. Since the pain began while playing football, were you able to continue the activity, or did it force you to stop immediately? Also, are you currently experiencing fever, nausea, vomiting, or changes in your bowel or bladder habits?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Only significant for asthma, well-controlled on medication. Social history: Unprotected sex with multiple partners. No use of tobacco, alcohol, or illicit drugs reported.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The history of unprotected sex with multiple partners significantly increases my concern for a gynecological or sexually transmitted infection-related cause. Given the pain started during physical activity, could you describe the character of the pain (sharp, dull, cramping) and whether you have noticed any vaginal discharge or bleeding? Additionally, have you experienced any pain specifically in the right lower quadrant?

REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Exam; REQUEST TEST: STI_Panel; REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: The recent measurements are normal, but the history of unprotected sex and the pain starting during physical activity raises concern for conditions like testicular torsion, ovarian torsion, or an appendicitis. Did the pain start specifically in the right lower quadrant, and did you notice any testicular swelling or vaginal bleeding? REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis; REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis_Repeat.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Appendicitis. The clinical picture of sudden-onset lower abdominal pain triggered by physical activity, combined with the exclusion of gynecological causes via ultrasound and a normal STI panel, strongly points to acute appendicitis.
